questions.q: What specific action does Griffin take against his landlord's house, and what immediate advantage does his invisibility give him during this event?
questions.a: Griffin deliberately sets fire to the house and then escapes unseen because he is invisible. A wrong answer (e.g., "the fire started accidentally" or "he fought the landlord") reveals the student has not grasped that the arson is a premeditated, malicious act facilitated by his scientific power.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why Griffin decides to burn the house. Use the phrase "lawless scientist" in your answer.
questions.a: Griffin burns the house out of revenge against the landlord who tried to eject him, and to destroy evidence of his experiments; this act makes him a lawless scientist who uses invisibility to commit crime without detection. A wrong answer that sympathises with Griffin ("he had no choice") reveals a misconception that the text justifies his violence — it does not; the narrator calls him "lawless" explicitly.

questions.q: Apply the "Action → Motivation → Consequence → Character Trait" pattern to the arson incident. Fill in each step with one phrase from the text.
questions.a: Action: "set fire to the house" | Motivation: "revenge" / "to get rid of the evidence" | Consequence: "wandering, invisible, homeless" | Character Trait: "lawless" (explicitly used by narrator). A wrong answer that swaps motivation and consequence shows the student cannot trace cause-effect in narrative sequence.

questions.q: Compare Griffin's response to the landlord's ejection notice with how a law-abiding citizen would respond. What does this comparison reveal about the theme "misuse of scientific discovery"?
questions.a: A law-abiding citizen would negotiate, pay dues, or seek legal help; Griffin chooses arson and invisible escape. This contrast reveals the theme: scientific power (invisibility) without moral restraint becomes a tool for lawlessness, not progress. A wrong answer that only lists differences without linking to the theme shows inability to connect character action to thematic statement.

questions.q: Evaluate this statement: "Griffin's invisibility forces him to become a criminal; he has no other choice." Defend your judgment with two pieces of textual evidence.
questions.a: The statement is false. Evidence 1: Griffin chooses "revenge" — the text says "to get his revenge he set fire to the house," indicating agency. Evidence 2: Later in London (next nodes) he steals clothes and food voluntarily, not from necessity alone. A wrong answer that agrees with the statement reveals a deterministic misconception that absolves Griffin of moral responsibility.

questions.q: Create a 3-sentence diary entry from the landlord's perspective the morning after the fire, showing his shock and suspicion. Use one word that reflects the story's Victorian setting.
questions.a: Example: "My lodgings are ash. The queer scientist vanished into thin air — no footprints, no trace, only the smell of petrol. I fear devilry, not mere mischief." A poor answer uses modern slang ("ghosted", "weird") or omits the landlord's perspective, showing failure to adopt historical voice and textual perspective.
